# Implementation plan — tasklet-alt

The architecture and build plan for tasklet-alt, generated by ProductForge. Every section cites
the spec IDs it rests on (R-, ADR-, INV-, E-, …) instead of re-deriving them; phases in `plans/`
cite these sections as §N.

## 1. Product overview

Provenance: generated by ProductForge from public research of Tasklet (https://tasklet.example); our design is independent.

tasklet-alt is task tracking for small teams. Parity: 14 BUILD NOW, 1 BUILD SIMPLIFIED, 3 USE EXTERNAL SERVICE, 11 DEFER, 2 DROP (spec/PARITY_MATRIX.md).

## 2. V1 scope

V1 covers R-001 to R-011; search, recurring tasks, integrations and the public API are deferred (SC-019, SC-007, SC-025).

## 3. Architecture

Next.js web, a Node API and a worker over PostgreSQL (ADR-005, ADR-010).

## 4. Technology stack

| Concern | Choice | ADR |
|---|---|---|
| Web | Next.js | ADR-010 |
| API and worker | Node.js | ADR-010 |
| Database | PostgreSQL | ADR-005 |

## 5. Repository structure

```text
tasklet-alt/
├── apps/
│   ├── web/
│   ├── api/
│   └── worker/
├── packages/
│   ├── db/
│   └── shared/
├── infra/
│   └── docker/
├── tests/
└── docs/
```

## 6. Data model

Workspaces, members, projects, tasks, comments, attachments and activity (E-01 to E-11); UUIDv7 keys (ADR-001).

## 7. Authentication

Authlane as the hosted identity provider (ADR-003, ADR-012).

## 8. Authorization

One policy module (ADR-004, INV-02).

## 9. Major subsystems

Workspaces, projects, tasks, board, comments, notifications, attachments, billing.

## 10. Integrations

Authlane, Payvault, Mailpost and Stowage (ADR-003, ADR-011, ADR-012 to ADR-015).

## 11. Async processing

Outbox and job queue (ADR-007).

## 12. Realtime behaviour

Polling every 30 s (ADR-006).

## 13. Search

Not in V1 (SC-019).

## 14. Security

INV-01, INV-02, INV-06.

## 15. Observability

Structured logs and error tracking.

## 16. Infrastructure

Managed PostgreSQL and object storage (ADR-005, ADR-008).

## 17. Deployment

Containers on a platform (ADR-009).

## 18. Cross-cutting invariants

INV-01 to INV-07.

## 19. Phase breakdown

| # | Phase | Depends on | Delivers |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00 | Repository foundation | none | A runnable monorepo skeleton with web, api and worker apps and a test harness. |
| 01 | Database and tenancy | 00 | PostgreSQL schema with workspace row-level security. |
| 02 | Sign-in | 01 | Members sign in through the identity provider. |
| 03 | Authorization policy | 02 | One policy module enforces the permissions matrix. |
| 04 | Workspaces and members | 03 | Owners create workspaces and invite members. |
| 05 | Projects | 04 | Members group tasks into projects with an owner. |
| 06 | Tasks and statuses | 05 | Tasks move through To do, In progress and Done with a history. |
| 07 | Board and polling | 06 | The board shows tasks by status and stays current within 30 s. |
| 08 | Comments and mentions | 06 | Members discuss tasks and mention each other. |
| 09 | Jobs and notifications | 08 | Assignments and mentions notify members in the app. |
| 10 | Attachments | 06 | Members attach files stored in object storage. |
| 11 | Billing | 04 | Owners manage the subscription through the payment provider. |
| 12 | Deployment and hardening | 07, 09, 10, 11 | Production images, encrypted stores and observability. |

## 20. Testing strategy

Unit and integration tests per phase; an end-to-end smoke test in phase 12.

## 21. Glossary

Workspace, member, project, task.
